page: Amazon Web Services m7g.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton3 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture with Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance and multi-core efficiency. The instance achieves a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3112.6, supported by strong uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths of 237.87 GB/sec and 109.3 GB/sec respectively. Multi-core processing is also a strength, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17159.0 and strong performance in PassMark CPU physics and database operations. However, single-core performance and specialized tasks like LLM text generation for small models or prompt processing for large models fall into average or poor categories, highlighting a performance tradeoff for single-threaded or heavy AI inference workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7g.8xlarge leverages the ARM-based Graviton architecture to deliver high resource density and strong memory bandwidth without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. This makes it highly suitable for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads. Recommended applications include static web serving, database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and general enterprise applications that benefit from balanced memory-to-CPU ratios and high memory throughput.
